narrative.overview: A calm reading page for bilingual engineering writing. The homepage says who you are, states a thesis in one line, lists the four pillars, shows the latest three articles, and offers an honest newsletter stub. Hierarchy comes from Source Serif 4 headings, an indented inner column, and hairline rules — not cards, boards, or motion.
keyCharacteristics: Ground #FAF9F6, ink #202522, soft ink #555B57, forest #315A49, rules #DCDDD8.
Source Serif 4 for site name and headings/titles; system sans for everything else.
Square layout; 3px radius only on form controls.
Light only; no transitions or animations.
Chrome English; per-post lang on titles and descriptions.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 for the site name, h1, h2, and article titles. System sans for body, meta, nav, and forms.

rules.name: The Forest Accent Rule
rules.body: Forest is for links, the primary button, and the focus ring. Soft ink carries secondary prose; never invent a third accent.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: Light-only. color-scheme: light; no dark theme.

rules.name: The Still Page Rule
rules.body: No CSS transitions or animations on the homepage. Hover is underline or a darker button fill only.

rules.name: The Frame and Inner Rule
rules.body: Section rules span the frame; article rules span the inner column. Indent shrinks before the gutter collapses below 40rem.

dos: **Do** keep chrome lang=en and put lang on post title/description.
**Do** announce language badges as Spanish/English to assistive tech.
**Do** explain disabled newsletter state in text, not colour alone.
**Do** keep the visible [Placeholder] marker while intro copy is provisional.
**Do** prefer rules and whitespace over cards, pills, and stat strips.
donts: **Don't** restore B612, board enamel, pillar strip paints, sequence numbers, or slide-out motion.
**Don't** add dark mode, client JS, or third-party font origins.
**Don't** put cards in the hero or first viewport clutter beyond brand, role, thesis, pillars, and the start of latest articles.
**Don't** use purple-on-white, cream-and-terracotta, or broadsheet newspaper defaults.
